name: Tokenized real-world assets
summary: Tokenization represents enforceable interests in funds, bonds and other assets on digital ledgers so issuance, transfer and settlement can be more programmable.
useCase: An eligible investor buys a tokenized Treasury fund and uses a permitted transfer or collateral workflow with identity, custody and redemption controls built in.
whyNow: CoinGecko’s defined tokenized-RWA universe grew from $5.42 billion at the start of 2025 to $19.32 billion on 31 March 2026. It excludes stablecoins and is dominated by a few asset categories; growth in token market value is not the same as issuer fee revenue or secondary-market liquidity. Institutional infrastructure is also changing: Securitize completed its public listing in July 2026. Forecasters disagree substantially about the eventual scale, and use different asset universes. The practical test is whether tokenization removes reconciliation, settlement or distribution costs while preserving legal rights. A token by itself does not make an illiquid asset liquid or ensure direct ownership of the underlying security.

mainstream.scope: Routine tokenized-fund, Treasury, collateral and selected securities workflows among regulated financial institutions and eligible investors.
mainstream.rationale: Short-duration funds and collateral have clearer operating uses than tokenizing every physical asset. Existing offerings can become repeatable as custody, cash settlement and market infrastructure mature. Legal fragmentation, limited liquidity and duplicate legacy systems can delay adoption. The date refers to selected workflows, not most global assets being on public blockchains.

metric.name: Tokenized RWA market capitalization, excluding stablecoins
metric.scope: CoinGecko’s covered tokenized Treasury, commodity, stock and ETF universe.
metric.limitations: A 15-month point-in-time comparison, not full-year growth. Coverage differs from RWA.xyz and bank forecasts. Asset prices, new listings and issuance affect the total. Tokenized derivatives trading volume is excluded and is not interchangeable with backed asset value.
metric.futureNote: No defensible comparable external deployment forecast found. The separate maturity path is an analyst scenario, not measured adoption.
metric.growthLabel: +256.7% in the covered universe over 15 months (CoinGecko)

milestones.text: Early tokenized funds existed, but no comparable full-universe annual market value was retained from the selected current dataset.
No harmonised annual non-stablecoin RWA observation retained; no missing value is interpolated.
No directly comparable annual value retained; pilot and product announcements are not substituted for assets outstanding.
McKinsey published a conditional 2030 tokenization estimate of about $2 trillion, illustrating growing institutional interest rather than observed adoption.
CoinGecko’s covered universe began the year at $5.42 billion; Tokeny became majority-owned by Apex Group.
The covered RWA universe reached $19.32 billion in March. Securitize completed its combination on 1 July and began trading as NYSE:SECZ on 2 July.

tailwinds: Digital cash, custody and identity infrastructure can support delivery-versus-payment workflows.
Fund administration and collateral movements contain repetitive reconciliation work that can be automated.
Established financial firms can distribute qualified products to existing clients.
bottlenecks: Legal rights, redemption, custody and insolvency treatment vary by instrument and jurisdiction.
A token can have a large outstanding value but little executable liquidity.
Parallel conventional systems can erase cost savings until workflows are sufficiently integrated.
watchMetrics: Assets outstanding net of double counting, split by legal instrument and issuer.
Unique funded investors, redemptions, executable secondary-market depth and settlement failures.
Measured operational cost and collateral efficiency versus the equivalent conventional workflow.
